title: `gl_compatibility` renderer crashes when a GDExtension addon owns a second native OpenGL (WGL) context on the main thread
body:
### Tested versions

4.7.1.stable (Windows 64-bit), non-Mono

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (nvlddmkm)

### Issue description

I have a `GDExtension` addon that creates its own independent native OpenGL context and window on Windows, via a statically-linked private copy of GLFW, using real WGL (`wglCreateContext`/`wglMakeCurrent`), not ANGLE. 

This window runs via the `_process()` callback on a `Node` subclass with set_process(true)`, i.e. on Godot's main/logic thread.

Each frame, the addon:
1. Saves the current WGL context/DC (`wglGetCurrentContext()`/ `wglGetCurrentDC()`), assumed to be the host's.
2. Handles its own GLFW window's events via `glfwPollEvents()`, which, per GLFW's documented behavior, processes the *entire calling thread's* Win32 message queue, not just messages for the addon's own window.
3. Switches to the addon's own GLFW window's WGL context (`glfwMakeContextCurrent`).
4. Issues its own GL draw calls.
5. Restores the host's previously-saved WGL context.

When the project's renderer is set to **`gl_compatibility`**, and my addon's window appears, the game crashes at an identical fault address, with no user input required. When I disable the addon's window is disabled, no crash occurs, all else being equal. This is reproducible on my end.

I think the underlying issue is that window messages - that are dispatched via `glfwPollEvents()` while my addon's context is current - trigger Godot's own renderer to issue GL calls while its context is not active.

I have tried reordering the addon's calls (pumping window events *before* switching to the addon's context) but this did not resolve the crash.

## Crash details

Captured via Windows crash dumps + `cdb.exe` (WinDbg CLI), `!analyze -v`:

```
FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: NULL_POINTER_WRITE_c0000005_msvcrt.dll!memcpy
ExceptionCode: c0000005 (Access violation)
Attempt to write to address 0000000000000000
```

Faulting call stack (all frames inside `Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64.exe`, no third-party/addon code in the crashing stack — offsets from `!analyze -v`, exact symbol names unavailable without engine PDBs):

```
msvcrt!memcpy+0x113
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x1538b0e
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x153bf80
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x3799370
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x3799593
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x327f2cd
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x3281b51
Godot_v4_7_1_stable_win64!NoHotPatch+0x337fe9d
... (down to RtlUserThreadStart)
```

This crash is reproducible across multiple separate runs, always at the same fault address.

## Possibly related issues

- [#85201](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/85201) — `gl_compatibility` crash on Windows/NVIDIA doing `memcpy` to a null pointer, originating from an unsynchronized `glMapBufferRange()` result during canvas instance-buffer upload. Notably the same crash signature (null-pointer `memcpy`) on the same renderer — we suspect this may point at the compatibility backend writing through a raw pointer into GL-driver-owned mapped memory without verifying/re-validating it, which would be consistent with that pointer becoming invalid if a WGL context switch happened at an unexpected moment.
- [#69836](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69836) — another `gl_compatibility` crash, `glDrawElements` in `rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp`.
- [#106853](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106853) — further Compatibility-renderer crashes tied to context/driver-layer issues.

## Additional notes

The addon's window works without issues when using the `forward_plus` renderer.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Set a project's renderer to `gl_compatibility`
2. Load a GDExtension addon that, from `_process()` (main thread), creates and drives its own independent native OpenGL context/window via a separate GLFW instance (real WGL on Windows), doing a per-frame save-context → poll-events → switch-context → draw → restore-context cycle as described above
3. Run the project
4. Crashes immediately after launch

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not available yet - I plan to build Godot from source to see if I can find the problematic code.
